title: Can PBR's 280,000-BPD Capacity Expansion Drive Cash Flow Growth? - The Globe and Mail
content: Brazil's state-run energy giant Petroleo Brasileiro S.A., or Petrobras (PBR), is increasing oil production by improving the efficiency of its existing offshore platforms. In its latest earnings call, management stated that 11 platforms have received authorization to operate above their original design capacity. These platforms now have approximately 280,000 barrels per day of additional production capacity. Petrobras achieved this increase without spending on new production platforms, although additional wells and subsea equipment are needed to use the available capacity. The initiative allows the company to increase production while limiting spending on new infrastructure. The improvements are already contributing to Petrobras' output. Through October 2026, the 11 platforms generated average incremental production of approximately 90,000 barrels per day. Petrobras has identified six more platforms for similar capacity increases, targeting another 260,000 barrels per day. Together, these initiatives offer the potential to add more than 500,000 barrels per day of production capacity. Management is working to connect additional wells and improve reservoir performance to make greater use of this capacity. The pace of these activities will determine how quickly the company can increase actual production. Building new offshore production facilities requires significant investment and several years before production begins. By increasing output from operating platforms, Petrobras can bring additional barrels to market sooner and avoid some spending associated with new facilities. Higher production from existing assets can support cash generation and improve capital efficiency, especially when oil prices remain favorable. However, the financial benefits will depend on how much additional production Petrobras achieves, the costs of connecting new wells and changes in crude prices. Petrobras’ offshore expansion highlights a broader challenge for oil producers: how to grow output while keeping development costs in check. U.S. energy majors ChevronCVX and ExxonMobil HoldingsXOM face the same trade-off, with Chevron expanding capacity at existing facilities and ExxonMobil looking to improve drilling productivity. Chevron is increasing production by expanding capacity at existing facilities through capital-efficient debottlenecking projects. In its latest earnings call, management said these projects have added more than 85,000 barrels per day of upstream capacity. Chevron has also increased processing capacity at Tengiz by 20% and facility capacity at Anchor by 33%. These improvements can support production growth while limiting investment in new infrastructure. Meanwhile, ExxonMobil is also focusing on improving operational efficiency to increase production and lower costs. In the Permian Basin, ExxonMobil is deploying automated drilling rigs to improve drilling performance and productivity. The company currently operates three such rigs and plans to expand their use to approximately 25% of its Permian fleet in 2027 and 50% by 2028. These improvements can help ExxonMobil increase production while managing development costs. Shares of PBR have gained around 27.6% over the past year, slightly underperforming the industry’s growth.
